summary: All three findings were confirmed and fixed, each with a regression test. The test reproduced the reviewer's bug; while writing it I also found a deadlock that already existed and fixed it. (1) Critical race: an in-progress snapshot's pins could be deleted. retain(live uuids) is replaced by SnapshotStorage::{copies, drop_copies(older_than)} and the policy now lives in api/snapshots.rs. A copy no recorded snapshot uses (keyed by snapshot uuid + index uuid) is dropped at once only when its snapshot can never be recorded: it was deleted, or it failed before the state was saved. Any other copy goes only once older than LEFTOVER_GRACE (1 h), and never while this process is still taking that snapshot (SnapshotData.taking). Restores are now tracked too (SnapshotData.restoring). Deleting a snapshot that is being restored answers 503 concurrent_snapshot_execution_exception with Elasticsearch's text, so a delete can't drop the pins a restore is reading (the same class of bug). (2) Leaked pins: snapshot create, clone and delete now sweep, and search-server sweeps in the background after each wake (NodeConfig.snapshot_leftover_grace). Pins of indices that were planned but not included are dropped right after recording. (3) Late indices: create_durable captures every index the snapshot will include before recording it. An index created or recreated in between is captured and the record is retried, so the 'recorded SUCCESS, then 500' path is gone. Deadlock found by the race test: persist refresh_policies and engines_and_states took ClusterData.shards and then the engine's index map, while opening an index takes them in the other order. A restore running alongside requests hung. Both now take the engine map first.
public_api: search-es engine::SnapshotStorage (async_trait): capture(snapshot, index_uuid, shards, Option<Arc<IndexEngine>>), load(snapshot, index_uuid, shards) -> Vec<SnapshotShard>, clone_snapshot(source, target, index_uuids), copies() -> EsResult<Vec<SnapshotCopy>>, drop_copies(&[SnapshotCopy], older_than: Option<Duration>) -> EsResult<()> (refused once unloaded). retain() is removed. New: engine::SnapshotCopy { snapshot: String, index_uuid: String, shard: u32 } (Clone, Eq, Hash). api::snapshots::{LEFTOVER_GRACE: Duration (1 h), sweep_leftover_copies(&Cluster, grace) -> EsResult<()>} (no-op without storage, and without any repository or repository data). search-server: NodeConfig.snapshot_leftover_grace: Duration (default LEFTOVER_GRACE), used by the background sweep after each wake. ClusterData implements copies() by listing snap.* pins, and drop_copies() reads written_ms when older_than is set. contracts.md is updated (the SnapshotStorage section and NodeConfig).
done: Finding 1, confirmed and fixed. crates/search-es/src/engine/mod.rs: the trait goes from retain to copies/drop_copies, plus SnapshotCopy. crates/search-es/src/api/snapshots.rs: SnapshotData.taking (Taking guard) and SnapshotData.restoring (RestoreGuard). drop_unused_copies decides what to drop: immediately if the caller's predicate says so, otherwise unrecorded, not taken here and older than the grace. create, clone and delete use it. A failed create or clone drops its own uuid's copies only when the closure failed (a failed save may have been persisted, so those are left to the sweep). The delete closure calls check_not_restoring: 503 concurrent_snapshot_execution_exception with the text '[default:<repo>:<snap>/<uuid>] cannot delete snapshot during a restore in progress in [RestoreInProgress[{<restore uuid>}{default:<repo>:<snap>/<uuid>}]]', from SnapshotsService.java and ConcurrentSnapshotExecutionException.java (9.1 source).

Regression test crates/search-server/tests/durability.rs concurrent_snapshot_deletes_keep_the_copies_of_snapshots_in_progress. It takes a 10-index x 2-shard snapshot while other requests repeatedly create and delete small snapshots and make failing creates. It then restores while deletes of the snapshot are attempted (about 1100 get 503) and checks every document comes back. With the old retain semantics the restored count was 0 of 3000; it passes 3 of 3 runs now.

Finding 2, confirmed and fixed. api::snapshots::sweep_leftover_copies runs after each wake in a tokio task (search-server node.rs load_inner, holding a Weak to the cluster). Snapshot create, clone and delete also sweep, all with the grace. Pins of indices that were planned but not included are dropped right after recording. Test durability.rs leftover_snapshot_copies_are_swept_after_the_grace_period writes a crashed-snapshot pin and a stray pin under a recorded snapshot. They survive snapshot operations and a wake with the default grace, and a node with grace 0 sweeps them while the recorded snapshots still restore.

Finding 3, confirmed and fixed. create_durable (snapshots.rs) plans the snapshot, captures the missing (index uuid, shards), then records inside an update closure that refuses if the snapshot now includes an uncaptured index uuid, and retries (up to 8 rounds). An index deleted and recreated under the same name is caught by uuid. Nothing is recorded before its copies exist.

Pre-existing deadlock fixed (crates/search-server/src/persist/mod.rs): refresh_policies called engine.apply_settings while holding self.shards, and engines_and_states called engine.indices_snapshot under self.shards. Engine::index holds indices.write and then ShardStorage::open locks shards (ABBA). Diagnosed with gdb through a privileged debian container, since the host has no gdb.
Unit test api::snapshots::tests::a_snapshot_being_restored_cannot_be_deleted: the message, status, repo scoping, and guard release for both the restoring and taking sets.

Docs: contracts.md (SnapshotStorage, sweep, NodeConfig field), compatibility.md (snapshot concurrency sentence in the round-4 wake-fidelity paragraph), the snapshots.rs module doc, the persist/mod.rs module doc.
remaining: Restore still treats a missing pin as an empty shard, because empty shards get no pin by design. A pin lost some other way (manual object deletion, a sweep bug) restores silently empty. Writing a marker pin for empty shards would make a missing pin detectable and let load fail with an error.

Snapshots are still not visible as IN_PROGRESS to concurrent GET _snapshot or _status while being taken (ES records SnapshotsInProgress in cluster state). roll completes them inside the request, so only concurrent observers see a difference.

Carried over: the published view falls back to showing everything after a merge that dropped a doc the searcher showed (merge over 2M docs, or over 100k listed docs); cross-cluster search statistics reset at a wake; an idle (5 min or more) unload commit doesn't count the flush ES's flushOnIdle would; _snapshot/_status file sizes are still placeholders (compat-es can now use the pins).
tests: cargo test -p search-server: unit 48, crash 2, differential 8, durability 19 (2 new), fairness 2, fencing 7, http 21, persist 13, store 1, all pass. search-es --lib snapshots: 5 pass, including the new a_snapshot_being_restored_cannot_be_deleted. search-store was not changed. cargo clippy --no-deps -p search-server -p search-store --all-targets -D warnings: clean. clippy --no-deps -p search-es --lib --tests: no warnings in my files. YAML on the final binaries: ES in memory 3809/3905 with 0 regressions (1 failure, 210_knn_search_profile, not durability); OpenSearch 1455/1506 with 0 regressions; ES durable (--data-dir) 3809 with 0 regressions; churn (--idle-unload-ms 1) 3809 with 0 regressions. Not rerun on S3 this round.
notes_for_others: compat-es (snapshots.rs): SnapshotStorage::retain is gone. To drop durable copies, call drop_unused_copies(cluster, store, predicate, LEFTOVER_GRACE): the predicate selects copies to drop now; everything else unrecorded is dropped only after the grace. A new path that writes pins before recording must hold a ctx.cluster.snapshot_data.taking(uuid) guard until the record is done, and a path that reads pins of a recorded snapshot (like restore) must hold snapshot_data.restoring(repo, name) so delete refuses with 503.

Everyone in search-server/persist and search-es engine: lock order is Engine.indices, then ClusterData.shards (Engine::index opens shards under indices.write). Never call engine methods (loaded, apply_settings, indices_snapshot, index) while holding ClusterData.shards.

Others' in-progress edits broke search-es compiles several times during this round (search/sort.rs id_fielddata_warning, search/join.rs is_empty on &Value, search/runtime.rs g::encode_latitude / json::java_double, SearchControl.ext). They were fixed by their owners within minutes.
No objects were created on roll-es-ref this round. A privileged debian:trixie-slim container was used briefly for gdb (--rm, -m 8g) and is gone.
